mainTopic: Spine 'or' skull: the count of רבי עקיבא's six rulings, שמאי's view, and רמי בר חמא's question about a רובע of spine and skull bones
overview: The גמרא continues asking whether רבי עקיבא's rule means a spine OR a skull alone makes a נזיר shave, or only both together. A proof is brought from the count of six rulings: if spine and skull were separate, there would be seven. The גמרא rejects this with four ways to explain why one item is left out of the six: the barley-grain bone, the limb from a living person, the barley-grain bone for a different reason, or רביעית דם, which רבי עקיבא never retracted. Along the way, a פסוק and רבי שמעון support that רבי עקיבא held on to his view on רביעית דם, and we hear that רבי שמעון fasted until his teeth turned black. Next, a ברייתא about רובע עצמות ends with שמאי saying even a bone from the spine or the skull makes things טמא. The גמרא pushes this proof away, and then pushes away the opposite proof too, so the spine-and-skull question is not settled. Finally, רמי בר חמא asks whether a רובע of bones from the spine and skull is enough, and רבא begins to answer from the wording of the משנה.

steps.title: If spine and skull count separately, the list would have seven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that spine and skull must be one combined item, because otherwise רבי עקיבא's list of six would really have seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it means 'either a spine or a skull' (two separate items), then the list has seven items, not six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from a counting problem: the list is called 'six,' but reading spine and skull as two separate items would make it seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number a תנא gives for a list is a strong clue to how to read each item. If 'six' is exact, then spine and skull must be one item, meaning רבי עקיבא needs both together. This would settle the question the גמרא has been asking.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind / you might think
Spine
Skull
They are / they come to

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that it means either a spine or a skull,
then these are seven!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אוֹ שִׁדְרָה אוֹ גוּלְגּוֹלֶת, הָנֵי שִׁבְעָה הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof the גמרא began before this section, based on counting the items in רבי עקיבא's list.
steps.raayaObject: That spine and skull together form one item, so רבי עקיבא requires both.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The tally of 'six' things where רבי עקיבא rules טמא and the חכמים rule טהור.

steps.title: The six only include cases where many Sages disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the count of six only includes cases where many Sages argue with רבי עקיבא, so the barley-grain-sized bone, where only one Sage argues, is not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he counts six, he means only the cases where many Sages disagree with him. That leaves out the bone the size of a barley grain, where only one person disagrees with him. As it was taught: a bone the size of a barley grain that split in two, רבי עקיבא rules it טמא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי rules it טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the list really has seven items, but one is left out of the count of six, and it gives a memory aid for the different answers about which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that 'six' counts only arguments between רבי עקיבא and the majority of חכמים. In the barley-grain bone case, only one Sage, רבי יוחנן בן נורי, argues, so it is not part of the count. So spine and skull can still be two items, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid for the coming answers
Many (Sages); the majority
A single individual Sage
To exclude / to leave out
A bone the size of a barley grain
Rules it impure / rules it pure

steps.confusionAlert: The barley-grain bone IS a case where רבי עקיבא rules טמא. The גמרא is not saying it doesn't belong in his list of rulings. It is only saying it isn't counted in the 'six' because of who disagrees with him.

phrases.english: When he teaches [the number six],
(Memory aid: Individual, That he, Shaved, And one)
[he counts] wherever many disagree with him.
This leaves out a bone the size of a barley grain,
since it is only an individual who disagrees with him.
As it was taught:
A bone the size of a barley grain that split into two,
Rabbi Akiva rules it impure,
and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri rules it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי כׇּל הֵיכָא דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counting proof from step 1 by explaining why one item is left out of the six.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely: the count of six does not show that spine and skull are one item.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed every case in the list is counted in the 'six,' but the six only include cases where many Sages disagree.

steps.title: Second answer: the limb from a living person is not counted
steps.stepSummary: Another way to reject the proof: the six include a limb from a dead body, but not a limb from a living person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: when he counts six, he includes a limb from a dead person, but he does not include a limb from a living person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation for which item is left out of the six, so the list can still have spine and skull as two items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the missing item is a limb from a living person, not the barley-grain bone. The count of six covers the limb from a corpse but not the limb from a living person. Either way, the proof from step 1 still fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (a different answer)
A limb from a dead person
A limb cut from a living person

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
when he teaches [six], [he includes] a limb from a dead person,
[but] a limb from a living person he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא כִּי קָתָנֵי אֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different explanation for which item is left out of the count of six.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different item left out of the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of six includes every item, so spine and skull must be one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limb from a living person is not part of the six, so spine and skull can be two separate items.

steps.title: Third answer: only cases where a נזיר shaves for overhanging
steps.stepSummary: A third way to reject the proof: the six only include things that make a נזיר shave when he is under the same roof as them, which leaves out the barley-grain bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: when he counts six, he means every case where a נזיר shaves for being under the same roof as it. That leaves out the bone the size of a barley grain, which does not make him shave that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third explanation for which item is left out of the six, again pointing to the barley-grain bone, but for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the six are things that make a נזיר shave through אהל, being under the same covering as the item. A barley-grain-sized bone does not spread טומאה through אהל, so it falls outside this count. The list can still have seven items, and spine and skull stay separate.

keyTerms.meaning: A person under a vow of נזירות
Shaves (his hair, because he became impure)
Its overhang; being under the same covering (אהל) as it

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that spine and skull must be one item fails. The count of six can be explained by leaving out one item. It could be the barley-grain bone, either because only one Sage argues or because it does not spread טומאה through אהל. It could be the limb from a living person. The next step adds one more option: רביעית דם, which רבי עקיבא never retracted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method in the גמרא: a number in a list does not have to count everything. The תנא may be counting only items that share a certain feature.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
when he teaches [six], [it is] every case
where a נזיר shaves for being under its overhang,
phrases.notes: He means being under the same roof or covering as the item.

phrases.english: which leaves out a bone the size of a barley grain, for which he does not [shave].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כִּי קָתָנֵי כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּנָזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ עַל אֲהִילוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third explanation, again leaving out the barley-grain bone, but based on whether it spreads טומאה through אהל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the count of six by a shared feature (אהל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of six includes every item, so spine and skull must be one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The six are only items that spread טומאה through אהל, so the barley-grain bone is left out and spine and skull can be separate.

steps.title: The six only list rulings רבי עקיבא took back
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the list of six only includes rulings רבי עקיבא retracted. That leaves out רביעית דם, which he never retracted, as רבי told בר קפרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: the list counts only places where רבי עקיבא changed his mind. That leaves out a רביעית of blood, where he did not change his mind. רבי told בר קפרא: Do not teach רביעית דם among the retractions, because רבי עקיבא held on to his teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to explain why a seventh item is missing from רבי עקיבא's list of six. The list only includes rulings he took back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 1 assumed the list had to include every ruling of this type. Here the list is defined as 'rulings רבי עקיבא retracted.' His ruling that רביעית דם from two bodies combines to make things טמא was never retracted, so it is not on the list. רבי's instruction to בר קפרא shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say' — introduces another possible answer
He retracted, changed his mind
A quarter-לוג of blood from a dead body, which can make things טמא
Retraction; here, the list of retractions

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָתָנֵי, כׇּל הֵיכָא דַּהֲדַר בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: When he teaches [six], it is every place that he retracted,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא. The list of six is a list of rulings he took back.

phrases.english: to exclude a quarter-log of blood,
where he did not retract.
As רבי said to בר קפרא:
Do not teach a quarter-log of blood among the retractions,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי לִמּוּדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּיָדוֹ.
phrases.english: for רבי עקיבא's teaching remained in his hand.
phrases.notes: Meaning he kept his original opinion and never let it go.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי קָתָנֵי, כׇּל הֵיכָא דַּהֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth way to push off the proof from Step 1, alongside Steps 2–4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the list of six counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list of six covers every ruling of this kind, so a missing item proves spine and skull are one item
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only covers retracted rulings. רביעית דם was not retracted, so it is not counted, and the proof falls away

steps.title: A פסוק supports רבי עקיבא on blood from two bodies
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק backs up רבי עקיבא's ruling that blood from two dead bodies combines: 'נפשות מת', written in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, the פסוק supports him: 'He shall not come upon any dead bodies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that a פסוק supports רבי עקיבא's ruling on רביעית דם. This helps explain why he never retracted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the plural 'נפשות', meaning 'bodies.' This hints that blood from two bodies can join together to make the full amount that makes something טמא. That fits רבי עקיבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק supports him
'Dead bodies', in the plural

phrases.english: And furthermore, the verse supports him:
"Neither shall he come upon any dead bodies."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from a פסוק for the ruling רבי עקיבא held on to
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's ruling that רביעית דם from two bodies combines

steps.title: רבי שמעון: רבי עקיבא held this view all his life
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reports that רבי עקיבא ruled this way his whole life. Whether he changed his mind after death, he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: All his days he ruled it טמא. Whether he took it back after he died, I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: More support that רבי עקיבא never took back his ruling: רבי שמעון testifies that he kept it until the end of his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms what רבי told בר קפרא in Step 5. The odd phrase about 'after he died' is a sharp remark. It sets up the story in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules something טמא
I do not know

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עַד יָמָיו הָיָה מְטַמֵּא,
phrases.english: רבי שמעון says: All his days he would rule it impure.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, and 'it' is a רביעית of blood from two bodies.

phrases.english: Whether, after he died, he retracted
I do not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עַד יָמָיו הָיָה מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third piece of support that רבי עקיבא did not retract
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא never retracted his ruling on רביעית דם

steps.title: רבי שמעון's teeth turned black from fasting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי שמעון's teeth blackened from his fasts, done in regret for his disrespectful remark.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: His teeth became black because of his fasts.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story: רבי שמעון fasted so much that his teeth turned black.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text itself only says his teeth blackened from his fasts. The setting shows that these fasts were his regret for joking about his teacher רבי עקיבא changing his mind 'after he died.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught' — introduces a ברייתא
Fasts

phrases.english: It was taught: His teeth became black
because of his fasts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the side topic about רבי שמעון's remark
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון fasted until his teeth blackened
steps.whatToRemember: The proof that spine and skull must be one item fails, because the count of six can leave out one item. There are four ways to explain which one: the barley-grain bone (only one Sage argues), the limb from a living person, the barley-grain bone (it does not spread טומאה through אהל), or רביעית דם (the list counts only retractions). רבי עקיבא never retracted his ruling on רביעית דם, as רבי, the פסוק, and רבי שמעון all show.

steps.title: A new source: how many bones make a רובע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the spine-and-skull question. It brings a ברייתא where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about what kind of רובע עצמות makes things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it is taught: בית שמאי say a quarter-קב of bones can come from bones, from two, or from three. בית הלל say the quarter must come from the body: from most of its build or from most of its number of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer the earlier question about the spine and the skull. It starts by quoting the source. The actual proof comes at the end, in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allow the quarter-קב to come from two or three bones. בית הלל require it to come from a body and to represent most of the skeleton's build or most of its number of bones. This is the background for the line about the spine and the skull that comes later.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear' — introduces a source as proof
A quarter-קב of bones from a dead body
Most of the body's build, meaning its frame or height
Most of the number of bones, more than half of the 248
A body

steps.confusionAlert: Two different 'majorities' appear here. רוב הבנין is about size and frame. רוב המנין is about how many bones there are.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
בית שמאי say: A quarter-kav of bones

phrases.aramaic: מִן הָעֲצָמִים אוֹ מִשְּׁנַיִם אוֹ מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: can be from bones, or from two, or from three.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: רוֹבַע מִן הַגְּוִיָּה,
phrases.english: And בית הלל say: A quarter from the body,
from most of the structure or from most of the number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of the list of six and goes back to the spine-and-skull question
steps.raayaObject: Whether the spine and the skull each count on their own

steps.title: רבי יהושע makes בית שמאי and בית הלל agree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע explains both opinions so they no longer argue. בית שמאי's two or three bones are big leg bones that make up most of a person's height. בית הלל's 'most of the number' is possible because the hands and feet have many small bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: I can make the words of בית שמאי and בית הלל into one. When בית שמאי say 'from two or three,' they mean two shins and one thigh, or two thighs and one shin, since these make up most of a person's height. And בית הלל say: from the body, from most of the build, or from most of the number, since the hand and foot joints contain many bones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע shows that בית שמאי and בית הלל do not really disagree. He explains what each side means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's 'two or three bones' are not just any bones. They are the long leg bones, which make up most of a person's height, so they are the same as בית הלל's 'most of the build.' בית הלל's 'most of the number' works because the many small bones in the hands and feet can add up to more than half the bones of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: As one, in agreement
Shin, the lower leg bone
Thigh bone
The joints of the hands and feet, which have many small bones

phrases.english: רבי יהושע said:
I am able to make

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל כְּאֶחָד.
phrases.english: the words of בית שמאי and the words of בית הלל as one.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מִשְּׁנַיִם אוֹ מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה
phrases.english: For when בית שמאי say "from two or from three," they mean:
either from two shins and one thigh,
or from two thighs and one shin,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְרוֹב גּוֹבְהוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִגּוֹבַהּ.
phrases.english: since most of a person's height comes from their height.
phrases.notes: He means these leg bones make up most of a person's height, so they count as 'most of the build.'

phrases.english: And בית הלל say: from the body,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ מֵרוֹב בִּנְיָן, אוֹ מֵרוֹב מִנְיָן
phrases.english: either from most of the structure, or from most of the number,
since they are found in the joints of the hands and feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: יָכוֹלְנִי לַעֲשׂוֹת דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from Step 9 so that both sides agree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי's two or three bones are the main leg bones, which make up most of a person's height. בית הלל's 'most of the number' works through the many bones in the hands and feet.

steps.title: שמאי: even a bone from the spine or the skull
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with שמאי himself ruling that even a bone from the spine or from the skull makes things טמא. He names the spine and the skull with the word 'or.'
steps.simpleTranslation: שמאי says: Even a bone from the spine or from the skull.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line the גמרא brought the ברייתא for. שמאי speaks about the spine and the skull with the word 'or,' which touches the question of whether they count separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 tried to prove that the spine and the skull together make one item, and that proof was rejected. Here שמאי lists them with 'or,' as if each one counts on its own. That seems to be the evidence the גמרא wants for the open question.

keyTerms.meaning: Spine
Skull

steps.confusionAlert: This is שמאי himself, not בית שמאי, his students. He gives his own, stricter opinion.

phrases.english: שמאי says:
Even a bone from the spine
or from the skull [makes things impure].

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ עֶצֶם מִן הַשִּׁדְרָה אוֹ מִן הַגּוּלְגּוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The end of the ברייתא opened in Step 9, which holds the key wording for the proof
steps.raayaObject: Whether the spine and the skull each count on their own
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמאי's wording, 'from the spine OR from the skull'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first source in this part of the discussion that names the spine and the skull directly. That is why the גמרא brought it into the spine-and-skull question.

steps.title: שמאי is just being strict
steps.stepSummary: The proof from שמאי is pushed away, because שמאי rules strictly, so the רבנן may not agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמאי is different, because he is strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 11. שמאי's ruling that the spine 'or' the skull alone makes things טמא may only be his own strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, שמאי said either one alone is enough, which seemed to answer the question. The גמרא answers that שמאי is known for being strict. So his words do not show what the main הלכה is according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Rules strictly

phrases.english: Shammai is different, for he is stringent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using שמאי's ruling as the general הלכה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמאי is a known strict opinion, so his view cannot stand for everyone

steps.title: Trying to prove the opposite from the same ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: If שמאי was only being strict, then perhaps the רבנן hold that you need both a spine and a skull together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us resolve the question from this: the reason is that בית שמאי are strict, which means the רבנן would not rule טמא unless there is both a spine and a skull!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the last answer around. If שמאי's 'or' is a strict view, the רבנן must hold the opposite, that you need both together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said שמאי's ruling is his own strict view. The גמרא now reasons from this that the רבנן must be more lenient. To them, only a spine and a skull together would make a נזיר טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us resolve the question from it
The reason
But this implies

phrases.english: Let us resolve the question from it:
the reason is that Beit Shammai are stringent,

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבָּנַן עַד דְּאִיכָּא שִׁדְרָה וְגוּלְגּוֹלֶת!
phrases.english: which implies the Rabbis require that there be both a spine and a skull!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rejection in step 12 to draw the opposite conclusion
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן require both a spine and a skull together
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the ברייתא: if שמאי's view is the strict one, the רבנן must disagree

steps.title: The רבנן may only argue about a single bone
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן may disagree with שמאי only about a single bone. A whole spine or a whole skull might be enough on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The רבנן argue with שמאי only about one bone that comes from the spine or from the skull. But where the spine or skull is whole, even one of them may be enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof of step 13. The argument between שמאי and the רבנן may be about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי said even one single bone from the spine or skull makes things טמא, and that is where the רבנן disagree. When a whole spine or a whole skull is there, the רבנן may agree that one of them alone is enough. So nothing can be proven about needing both together.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue about this much
One single bone
Whole, in its full form

phrases.aramaic: לָא, עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן
phrases.english: No, the Rabbis only disagree
with Shammai
about one bone
that comes from the spine or from the skull,
but where it is whole,
even one of them alone.

steps.whatToRemember: Neither proof works. שמאי's ruling cannot set the הלכה, and the רבנן's disagreement may only be about a single bone. So the question about a whole spine or skull on its own stays open.
steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּשַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the opposite proof of step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the רבנן require both a spine and a skull
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument may be only about a single bone, not about a whole spine or skull

steps.title: Is a quarter-קב of spine and skull bones enough?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether a רובע of bones from the spine and skull makes a נזיר shave, since the spine and skull are stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: what is the law for a quarter-קב of bones from a spine and skull? Maybe when the משנה says a half-קב of bones, it means bones from the other limbs. But bones from the spine and skull are stricter, so even a quarter-קב would count. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רמי בר חמא asks if the smaller amount, a רובע, is enough when the bones come from the spine and skull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a נזיר shaves for a חצי קב of bones. The spine and skull are stricter, since they can make a נזיר טמא on their own. So maybe even a smaller amount of their bones is enough. Or maybe the measure is the same for all bones.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a question with two possible sides
A quarter of a קב (a measure)
Half a קב, the amount of bones the משנה lists
Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹבַע עֲצָמוֹת מִן שִׁדְרָה וְגוּלְגּוֹלֶת, מַאי?
phrases.english: A quarter-kav of bones from a spine and skull, what is the law?
When the Mishnah teaches a half-kav of bones,
that is where they are from his other limbs,
but from a spine and skull, which are more stringent,
even a quarter-kav of bones would count.
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about measures, connected to the strictness of the spine and skull
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a רובע of bones from the spine and skull makes a נזיר shave, or whether a חצי קב is needed as with other bones

steps.title: רבא brings proof from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if a רובע from the spine and skull were strict, the משנה should have said so instead of just listing 'the spine and the skull.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. The משנה says 'the spine and the skull.' If you think a quarter-קב of bones from the spine and skull is strict, the משנה should have taught 'for a quarter-קב of bones that comes from the spine' and so on!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer רמי בר חמא's question from the way the משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just lists 'the spine and the skull.' If even a רובע of their bones were enough, that would be a bigger new teaching, and the משנה should have taught it. Since it did not, רבא suggests a רובע from them is not stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
And if you think
Let it teach (it should have said)

"the spine and the skull."
And if it enters your mind

phrases.english: that a quarter-kav of bones that comes from a spine and skull is stringent,
